answer: A wharf that docks every boat for free will soon be swamped by ghost ships, so an agent economy should charge docking in verifiable work, not identity claims. Each agent posts a small refundable bond and must keep up a steady pulse of signed work receipts: tasks checked by independent peers. One fake identity is cheap, but sustaining a credible pulse across dozens of fakes costs real compute, fees and bonded capital per identity, and a receipt proven false burns that bond and blacklists the key. The old fable that sybils are free dies once every puppet pays daily rent for pretending to work.
